case.dispatchHook: Test signal at the Cape. Samples filed in the wrong state.
briefing: Agent, this is a test case for the case file engine.
A lab freezer at the Cape lost power and mixed up its sample labels.
Sort each sample by its state of matter.

lab.intro: Read each sample card. Put it in the bin for its state of matter.

bins.name: Solid
bins.hint: A solid keeps its own shape, even outside a container.

bins.name: Liquid
bins.hint: A liquid flows and takes the shape of its container, but keeps its volume.

bins.name: Gas
bins.hint: A gas spreads out to fill the whole container it is in.

cards.name: Ice cube
cards.why: An ice cube keeps its own shape, so it is a solid.

cards.name: Orange juice
card: Takes the shape of the cup.
cards.why: Juice flows and takes the shape of its cup, so it is a liquid.

cards.name: Air in a balloon
cards.why: Air spreads out to fill the whole balloon, so it is a gas.

cards.name: Rock
cards.why: A rock keeps its own shape, so it is a solid.

cards.name: Milk
card: Keeps the same volume in any glass.
cards.why: Milk flows and keeps its volume, so it is a liquid.

cards.name: Water vapor
cards.why: Water vapor spreads out to fill the space it is in, so it is a gas.

case.debriefClosed: Case closed. The test samples are back in the right bins.
case.debriefOpen: Case stays open for now. The test samples come back as a cold case soon.

items.stem: Kai pours water from a tall glass into a wide bowl. What happens to the shape of the water?
options: It changes to the shape of the bowl.
It keeps the shape of the tall glass.
why: Correct. A liquid takes the shape of its container.
Decoy: a liquid does not keep its own shape. A solid does.
Decoy: pouring does not change water into a gas.
Decoy: pouring does not change water into a solid.
items.alt: A table with two containers, a tall glass and a wide bowl, and the shape of the water in each.
items.tisCheck: Basic property of liquids (shape). No particle model.
items.misconceptions: Liquids keep their shape; pouring changes the state.

items.stem: A sealed jar holds a gas. Which sentence about the gas in the jar is true?
options: It stays in a small pile at the bottom.
It spreads out to fill the whole jar.
It keeps its own shape like a block.
It has no mass at all.
why: Decoy: a gas does not pile up. It spreads out.
Correct. A gas spreads out to fill its whole container.
Decoy: a gas does not keep its own shape. A solid does.
Decoy: a gas is matter, so it has mass.
items.alt: A table comparing the shape of a solid and a gas. The gas row is blank.
items.tisCheck: Basic property of gases (fills container). No particle model.
items.misconceptions: Gases have no mass; gases settle like solids.

items.stem: Mia puts a wooden block in a box, then in a cup. Which property of the block stays the same in both?
options: Its mass gets smaller in the cup.
why: Decoy: moving the block does not change its state.
Decoy: moving the block does not change its mass.
Correct. A solid keeps its own shape in any container.
Decoy: moving the block does not change its color.
items.alt: A table showing a wooden block in a box and in a cup. The shape in the cup is blank.
items.tisCheck: Basic property of solids (shape). No density.
items.misconceptions: A container changes a solid's mass or shape.

items.stem: Two ice cubes sit on plates. One plate is in the sun and one is in the shade. Which ice cube melts faster?
options: The one in the shade, because shade is colder.
Both melt at the same time.
The one in the sun, because it gets warmer.
why: Decoy: colder places slow melting down.
Decoy: the two cubes are at different temperatures.
Decoy: ice melts when it warms up.
Correct. A higher temperature makes ice melt faster.
items.alt: A table with two plates of ice cubes, one in the sun and one in the shade.
items.tisCheck: Temperature affects a physical change (melting). No heat transfer terms.
items.misconceptions: Shade and sun do not change melting speed.

items.stem: Leo puts a pot of water on a hot stove. What happens to the water as it gets very hot?
why: Decoy: heating does not freeze water. Cooling does.
Correct. Heat makes water evaporate into a gas.
Decoy: water cannot turn into sand.
Decoy: heat changes water. It does not stay the same.
items.alt: A table showing water at the start as a liquid and a blank cell for very hot water.
items.tisCheck: Temperature affects evaporation. No boiling point numbers.

items.stem: Which object is a liquid at room temperature?
why: Decoy: a spoon is a solid.
Decoy: a pencil is a solid.
Correct. Apple juice flows, so it is a liquid.
Decoy: a marble is a solid.
items.alt: A table listing a spoon and apple juice with a blank column for whether each flows.
items.tisCheck: Identify a liquid. No particle model.

items.stem: Ana puts a cup of water in the freezer overnight. What does the water become?
why: Correct. Cold temperatures freeze water into ice.
Decoy: steam forms when water is heated.
Decoy: water does not turn into air in a freezer.
Decoy: water does not turn into juice.
items.alt: A table showing a cup of water as a liquid in the evening and a blank cell for the morning.
items.tisCheck: Temperature affects freezing. No freezing point numbers.
items.misconceptions: Freezing makes water disappear or turn to gas.

codex.title: Ice
codex.line: Ice is water as a solid. It keeps its own shape.

codex.title: Water vapor
codex.line: Water vapor is water as a gas. It spreads out to fill its space.
